newsitem.title: FRANCE: Broker Leven turns buy on Scor.
newsitem.headline: Broker Leven turns buy on Scor.

text.p: Broker Leven said on Wednesday it had changed its recommendation on French reinsurance group Scor to "buy" from "neutral".
Scor shares continued to benefit from speculation Scor could become the target of a bid following news Swiss Re was buying reinsurer Mercantile & General from Prudential Corp.
Scor shares gained six francs to 208 francs at 1446 GMT, having hit a day-high of 213.8 francs.
In a research note Leven analyst Benoit Vincenzi set a target of 260 francs for the stock, taking into account limited liquidity, that is a price/earnings ratio of 11.3 for 1996.
The M&G deal has "renewed speculation the group could be a buy target for a large US reinsurer," the analyst said.

He said the group should be able to maintain good profitability (of some 10 percent) in 1995, citing "satisfactory price conditions, capacity to absorb a higher damage rate and market share gains linked to external growth,"

Vincenzi put net attributable profit at 623 million francs in 1996 and 677 million francs in 1997, that is net earnings per share of 23 francs and 25 francs, respectively. Net profit was 522 million francs in 1995.
UAP has a 40.9 percent stake in Scor. The French insurer said in June it may cut that stake when Scor is listed in New York possibly in September.
Other Scor shareholders are AGF with less than five percent of capital, Axa (seven percent), mutual insurers (around 10 percent) and Swiss Life (2.25 percent).
Leven sees arbitrage opportunities at 260/280 francs when the stock is listed in the United States.
In a research note dated August 21 De Bouzet brokerage said the stock had the potential to rise to 250 francs per share.
It said the stock's potential "lies more in its capacity to maintain already healthy profitability than in a takeover scenario in a sector where the cards have already been largely redealt,".
